text:
sanjay: seeing a weird sawtooth of Xid 13 spikes on a subset of A10 cards in eu-west1 this morning. per-card failure rate jumped ~3x at 03:10-03:40 UTC.

maria: saw that too. different tenants but similar op mix: lots of streaming decode + short-context generation (<=128).

ops-bot: alert: node-gpu-az3-042 reported `Xid 13` 7 times in 30m — auto-log-collected (/var/log/nvidia/xid.log).

lydia: can you paste the last dmesg snippet? wondering if there's a PCIe reset preceding the Xid.

sanjay: pasted logs ->
```
[Mar 18 03:12:09] nvidia: Xid (13: INTERNAL): channel 00000001ff
[Mar 18 03:12:09] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: id=0010
[Mar 18 03:12:09] pcie_aspm: can not change L1->L0 state
[Mar 18 03:12:12] nvidia: GPU reset successful
```

maria: interesting — AER events right before Xid 13. that suggests link noise / NIC interrupts. which topo is this rack on?

ricardo: rack is on top-of-rack switch fw 2.1.8, Mellanox NICs, same cohort that had transient resets last week but lower volume.

tom: correlated by op-type: Xid 13 rate per million tokens = 0.9 for streaming decode, 0.15 for embed. So decode-heavy tenants are impacted.

lydia: hypothesis: small-batch, high-concurrency streaming keeps NVLink active with short kernels causing heat/voltage transients + PCIe AER. maybe driver/kernel combo on our 6.2 hwe.

maria: any recent flaps in fabric? I see packet drops on toprack logs 03:09-03:15 for that leaf.

ops-bot: metric: card-death-rate (last 24h) on node-gpu-az3-042 = 4.1 per million requests, baseline 0.8.

sanjay: proposed immediate actions: 1) soft-drain node-gpu-az3-042 from serving pools for 12h; 2) enable verbose AER + kernel probe on that host; 3) increase Xid histogram retention in datadog for 48h. ok?

tom: +1 to soft-drain. but note capacity in eu-west1 is only 85% spare — will push some tenants to other regions, may bump latency. we should flag customer-impact.

maria: ops: run `sudo nvidia-smi -q -d PIDS,ECC,UTILIZATION` and stash output in /tmp/xid-2139876543/ ; also capture `ethtool -S` from NIC.

ricardo: scheduler: I'll shift low-SLA jobs and hold high-SLA to dedicated pool. Also starting rotation test on two sibling nodes to see if pattern follows the PCIe lane.

lydia: for longer term: add a per-optype Xid 13/31/48 split in the infra dashboards, and correlate with sequence length and batch size. we should also test driver 525.x vs 535.x on a canary to see if AER behavior changes.

sanjay: agree. also put card on hardware review list if we see >5 resets in 48h. replacement cost vs availability tradeoff — ping finance for hot spares budget?

maria: quick note: we saw Xid 48 earlier but on INT8 quantized embedder workloads on a different cohort. that one had NV firmware mismatch. keep separate but add cross-correlation.

ops-bot: action logged: ticket INFRA-3482 created (soft-drain + verbose-logs).

tom: will follow up with a short postmortem if we hit auto-replace threshold. for now: drain + logs + driver canary.

ricardo: FYI running `watch -n 10 'grep Xid /var/log/nvidia/xid.log | tail -n 50'` on the host yields repeated Xid 13 clusters every ~3-4 minutes.

lydia: if AER is the root cause, root fix may be switch port lane reconfiguration or NIC firmware. schedule with networking team after we confirm.

sanjay: ok team — executing plan now. will update thread with datadog dashboard link and logs. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks, keep the customer comms looped in (ops-ct).

ops-bot: update: logs uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/2139876543/ (permissions: eng-sre,eng-infra).

sanjay: attaching quick findings summary for ticket ->
- symptom: repeated Xid 13 on subset of A10 cards in eu-west1
- immediate: soft-drain nodes, capture AER/PCIe/NIC stats, shift low-SLA traffic
- hypothesis: PCIe AER/link noise triggered by fabric packet issues under small-batch streaming workload
- next: driver canary, NIC fw check, replace if >5 resets in 48h

maria: readable and concise. thanks.

ricardo: I'm scheduling a maintenance window for NIC fw check tomorrow 02:00 UTC if no further regressions.

sanjay: thread closed for now, will reopen if replacements happen.
